text.p: Italy's mobile phone consortium Omnitel, where Olivetti has a 35.5 percent stake, said it had gained 713,000 mobile phone subscribers in the 13 months since the group launched its service in December 1995.

In the 13 months since its start-up in December 1995, Omnitel's coverage of territory had risen to almost 60 percent from 40 percent, which represented a 90 percent coverage of Italy's population, a group statement said.
During 1996, Omnitel took on an extra 1,282 employees to bring its total workforce to 2,850 by the end of 1996, of which half are dedicated to assisting clients.

Omnitel's managing director Silvio Scaglia said the group's success was based on the quality of its service and client assistance. "We must continue to improve the standard of service alongside growth which will continue to be exceptional," he said.
Subcribers to Omnitel's GSM digital network reached 560,000 by end-September 1996, and it had then forecast 700,000 by the year-end.

Omnitel's competitor, state-controlled Telecom Italia Mobile (TIM), launched a GSM service in early 1995 and gained 1.1 million GSM subscribers by mid-October. Its total number of subscribers -- including GSM digital and analogue subscribers -- at that date was close to five million.
Investment house SBC Warburg today estimated that the number of TIM subscribers would rise to 5.7 million by the end of 1996.
